items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026
items.q: I can’t remember if it was Leonard Cohen or Bob Dylan said that the music is up there and we just bring it down.

ctx.x: People want to stand next to them because they make you feel better.

Well it’s their vibration that they –the frequency that they vibrate from. You know? They said, I can’t remember if it was Leonard Cohen or Bob Dylan said that the music is up there and we just bring it down. You know? Musicians bring it down. And I do believe that with all my heart. You know? They are healers. You know? The musicians are the healers of the world and I can’t imagine getting through life, and I always used to say that to our audience, you know they were there when you fell in love and they were…
Do you consider yourself an optimist?

items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I missed all the Bob Dylans and the Odettas, and all that live music scene.

ctx.x: I don’t know exactly what years we’re talking about, but it was a very different time, and the Village was a very different place.

Yeah, I came, sadly, at the tail end of that. I missed the glory moments. I missed all the Bob Dylans and the Odettas, and all that live music scene. Most of the people we ended up helping, and a lot of the legends, I never got to hear them in person. Which is painful. But I caught a few.
So after the Swiss ladies, you’re living with these two dancers on 10th Street, and at 17 you have an injury to your knee...
